'''Boris Tsygan''' is a mathematician prominent in [[noncommutative geometry]] who is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Northwestern University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boris Tsygan's Homepage |url=https://sites.math.northwestern.edu/~tsygan/ |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=sites.math.northwestern.edu}}</ref> He performed his undergraduate studies at [[Kiev State University]] concluding in 1980 and earned his PhD in [[pure mathematics]] at [[Moscow State University]] in 1987. He is credited with independently discovering [[cyclic homology]] along with [[Alain Connes]].<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Tamarkin |first1=Dmitri |title=Noncommutative differential calculus, homotopy BV algebras and formality conjectures |date=2000-02-15 |eprint=math/0002116 |last2=Tsygan |first2=Boris }}</ref> He was advised by prominent mathematician [[Yuri Manin]] when earning his PhD.

== Research ==
Much of Tsygan's research has been centered around [[cyclic homology]], but he has also contributed to several other branches of mathematics. Notably, he is namesake of the Tsygan Formality Conjecture<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Shoikhet |first=Boris |date=2003-10-15 |title=A proof of the Tsygan formality conjecture for chains |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=179 |issue=1 |pages=7–37 |doi=10.1016/S0001-8708(02)00023-3 |doi-access=free |issn=0001-8708}}</ref> and has studied [[K-theory]] with [[Boris Feigin]].
